title: How many notes of each kind can the shop money make?
description: Harpreet's father counts the day's money in a sweet shop in Amritsar. The video finds the notes of ten, one hundred, five hundred and the thousands by hiding digits.
teaching_notes: One idea: hiding digits on the right counts tens, hundreds and thousands; notes of five hundred come from grouping hundreds in fives. Watch for a child who reads one digit instead of everything to its left.

source: Let Us Do (second set) 9 (a) to (d), notes in 7,934
video_script.why: The child can read a number but has not yet counted how many tens, hundreds and thousands it holds in all.
video_script.substitution: Hide the digits on the right to count each kind of note; group the hundreds in fives for notes of five hundred.
video_script.anchor: Harpreet's father counting the day's money in his sweet shop in Amritsar
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu reads the hundreds digit nine as the count. The count of hundreds includes all the thousands too, seventy nine in all.
video_script.payoff_line: hide the digits on the right

final_answer.value: 793 notes of 10, 79 notes of 100, 7 thousands and 15 notes of 500
final_answer.spoken: fifteen notes of five hundred and seven thousands

maths_rules: 7,934 rupees: hide 1 digit leaves 793, so 793 notes of 10 with 4 left
hide 2 digits leaves 79, so 79 notes of 100 with 34 left
slip: the hundreds digit 9 gives 9 notes of 100 = 900, far below 7,934
hint example: 250 gives 25 tens and 2 hundreds
video_script.design: Exercise. Hint: hide the last digit for tens, the last two for hundreds. A small box of 250 rupees shows it before the child tries again.

beats.on_screen: a photo of the pile of rupee notes sits behind as a dimmed backdrop and fades at the end of the beat; a small title card From your book; a sweet shop counter with a money box marked 7,934 rupees; four empty boxes labelled notes of 10, notes of 100, thousands and notes of 500

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.story: a money box with 7,934 rupees appears at the shop
marks.ask: four empty boxes appear: notes of 10, notes of 100, thousands, notes of 500

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='story'/>Harpreet's father runs a sweet shop in Amritsar. He counts the day's money, seven thousand nine hundred and thirty four rupees.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many notes of ten and of one hundred are in it? How many thousands, and how many notes of five hundred?

beats.on_screen: the items hold still and the anchor gets an accent underline

marks.stop: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

beats.on_screen: a small money box of 250 rupees: hiding the last digit leaves 25 notes of 10; hiding the last two digits leaves 2 notes of 100; a hint note appears

marks.ex: 250 rupees appears in a small box
marks.hunds: hiding the last two digits leaves 2

narration: <bookmark mark='ex'/>Take two hundred and fifty rupees.
<bookmark mark='tens'/>It makes twenty five notes of ten.
<bookmark mark='hunds'/>It also makes two notes of one hundred, with fifty left over.
<bookmark mark='hint'/>Hide the last digit to count tens, and the last two digits to count hundreds. Try again with this.

beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows 9 notes of 100 from the hundreds digit of 7,934; nine 100 notes = 900 appears beside 7,934; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.chintu: Chintu's bubble appears with the wrong count
marks.strike: the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>The hundreds digit is nine, so there are nine notes of one hundred.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>Nine notes of one hundred are only nine hundred rupees.
<bookmark mark='more'/>The money is seven thousand nine hundred and thirty four, which is much more than that.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>Each thousand alone holds ten notes of one hundred.

beats.on_screen: the rule line appears; 7,934 with the last digit hidden shows 793; with two digits hidden shows 79; with three digits hidden shows 7

marks.hunds: 7,934 with 34 hidden shows 79 and the box notes of 100 shows 79
marks.thou: 7,934 with 934 hidden shows 7 and the box thousands shows 7

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Hide the digits on the right, and read what is left.
<bookmark mark='tens'/>Hiding the four leaves seven hundred and ninety three.
<bookmark mark='tens2'/>That means seven hundred and ninety three notes of ten.
<bookmark mark='hunds'/>Hide the last two digits. Seventy nine is left, so there are seventy nine notes of one hundred.
<bookmark mark='thou'/>Hide the last three digits, and seven is left. That is seven thousands.

beats.on_screen: 79 hundreds are grouped in fives: 79 = 15 × 5 + 4; the box notes of 500 shows 15

marks.start: 79 hundreds appear as a row of blocks
marks.five: the blocks are grouped in fives
marks.fifteen: 15 groups of five and 4 loose blocks appear

narration: <bookmark mark='start'/>For notes of five hundred, start from the seventy nine hundreds.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Every five hundreds make one note of five hundred.
<bookmark mark='fifteen'/>Seventy nine hundreds hold fifteen fives, with four hundreds left over.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>That makes fifteen notes of five hundred.

beats.on_screen: a check: 15 × 500 = 7,500, and 7,934 − 7,500 = 434 is less than one more note of 500
narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>To check, multiply back. Fifteen notes of five hundred make seven thousand five hundred rupees.
<bookmark mark='left'/>The rest, four hundred and thirty four, is less than one more note of five hundred.
